# Endpoint and dataset inventory

What the apps contact while a reader uses them, what the build depends on,
and the terms on each. **Generated** — see the generator's docstring for
which file each figure is read from, and why none of them is restated here.

## 1. Runtime endpoints — what the browser contacts

Hosts are extracted from each instance's own `index.html` and `sw.js` and
classified by **path shape**, which is what separates a request this site
makes from a link a reader clicks. Of **336 distinct hosts** those files
name, **45 are fetched by the browser**; the other 291 are links.

### Geocoder — 3 host(s)

| host | instances |
|---|---|
| `geosearch.planninglabs.nyc` | ny |
| `nominatim.openstreetmap.org` | il, ca, wi, ia, mi, mn, ky, in, nc, ok, sc, tn, ar, ms, la, mo, va, wv, ga, pa, nv, az, nj, nh, tx, fl, oh, wa, ma, co, md, al, or, ct, ut, ks, nm, ne, id, hi, me, mt, ri, de, sd, nd, ak, vt, wy |

The most sensitive flow on the site: it is **the text a reader

each one's policy; this table is held to that generator's own
per-app measurement, so the two cannot disagree.

### Map-link lookup — 1 host(s)

| host | instances |
|---|---|
| `link-lookup.districtry.deno.net` | il, ny, ca, wi, ia, mi, mn, ky, in, nc, ok, sc, tn, ar, ms, la, mo, va, wv, ga, pa, nv, az, nj, nh, tx, fl, oh, wa, ma, co, md, al, or, ct, ut, ks, nm, ne, id, hi, me, mt, ri, de, sd, nd, ak, vt, wy |

districtry's own service (`services/link-lookup/main.ts`, on Deno
Deploy). It receives **a short Google Maps or Apple Maps link**, and
only when a reader pastes one or shares one into the installed app,
and answers with the full link it leads to.
Every app also sends it, at `?a=`, **the street address a reader searches for
or a map link carries** when the map's own search can't find the house,
and it asks the U.S. Census Bureau's geocoder where that number falls.
The il, ny, ca, wi, ia, mi, mn, ky, in, nc, ok, sc, tn, ar, ms, la, mo, va, wv, ga, pa, nv, az, nj, nh, tx, fl, oh, wa, ma, co, md, al, or, ct, ut, ks, nm, ne, id, hi, me, mt, ri, de, sd, nd, ak, vt and wy apps send it **the public address of an office a card shows** too,
when the app's office-pin geocoder can't place that office's pin, which
says which district the reader selected.
No served file names the Census host, because only the lookup asks it.
`build_privacy_page.py` names the lookup and the Census Bureau as
recipients.

### File host — 1 host(s)

| host | instances |
|---|---|
| `files.districtry.com` | il, ny, ca, wi, ia, mi, mn, ky, in, nc, ok, sc, tn, ar, ms, la, mo, va, wv, ga, pa, nv, az, nj, nh, tx, fl, oh, wa, ma, co, md, al, or, ct, ut, ks, nm, ne, id, hi, me, mt, ri, de, sd, nd, ak, vt, wy |

districtry's own Cloudflare R2 bucket, holding the vector-tile
archives and the Census block populations, which GitHub Pages no
longer publishes. A map reads an archive a byte range at a time and
a population file per county a comparison touches, on the live site
only; a copy run anywhere else reads its own files.
`deploy-pages.yml` copies the files there and reads a sample back;
`build_privacy_page.py` names Cloudflare as their recipient.

### Webfonts — none

**No external font host.** Barlow is self-hosted per instance, and
`check_no_webfont_host()` fails the build if that stops being true —
a font CDN would be a recipient the privacy page does not name.

### Where each layer's shapes come from

Measured **2026-10-11** in a real browser by `scripts/probe_layer_sources.mjs`,
which switches each layer on alone and reads every response the page
fetches from another host. A layer **fetches** its shapes when a response
carries polygon or line geometry: either the whole set, downloaded once
and tested in the browser, or only the district at the selected point,
asked of the server. A county-dispatched layer is also measured one county
at a time. A weekly workflow (`update-layer-sources.yml`) re-runs it and
opens a pull request when a result changes, but **nothing fails when this
is stale**, so a layer added since that date is named below as not
measured until the next run describes it.

**258 distinct source hosts** across the six manifests. Each instance's
`validate_sources.py` is the authority — it carries every dataset id and
provenance URL the build depends on, and is machine-checked monthly. Two
entry classes mean the source refuses this client, and the check
**inverts** for both: the refusal is expected and its LIFTING is the signal
a human can act on. They differ in whether anything is fetched. A
`blocked` entry was measured unreachable and IS re-probed, because probing
is how you learn an outage ended. A `robots_declined` entry is a host whose
own robots.txt asks this client not to read it, and is NEVER fetched — the
request is the thing being asked for, so only robots.txt is re-read.

## 3. Terms

[`LICENSE-DATA.md`](../LICENSE-DATA.md) is the authority and the terms are **not**
restated here — restating a licence is how two copies come to disagree
about what a publisher granted. Code is Apache 2.0; the compiled databases
are ODbL v1.0, a grant over *the compilation* and explicitly not over the
underlying records. The categories of underlying terms it records:

- [1. United States federal works — public domain](../LICENSE-DATA.md#1-united-states-federal-works-public-domain)
- [2. State, county and municipal public records](../LICENSE-DATA.md#2-state-county-and-municipal-public-records)
- [3. Jo Daviess County board districts — licensed, display-only, NOT redistributable](../LICENSE-DATA.md#3-jo-daviess-county-board-districts-licensed-display-only-not-redistributable)
- [4. The *Wisconsin Blue Book* — used by permission, on terms the Bureau stated](../LICENSE-DATA.md#4-the-wisconsin-blue-book-used-by-permission-on-terms-the-bureau-stated)
- [5. Grundy County fire, library and park districts — derived, and the county's answer on record](../LICENSE-DATA.md#5-grundy-county-fire-library-and-park-districts-derived-and-the-countys-answer-on-record)
- [6. Whiteside County fire and park districts — derived, shown with the county's written permission](../LICENSE-DATA.md#6-whiteside-county-fire-and-park-districts-derived-shown-with-the-countys-written-permission)

See also its [Attribution](../LICENSE-DATA.md#attribution) and [Warranty](../LICENSE-DATA.md#warranty)
sections. Two runtime things that document deliberately does not cover are
the map tiles and the geocoding, both of which run on OpenStreetMap data;
it also records that **no shipped boundary is derived from OpenStreetMap**.

### Where a term is recorded, and where it is not

Per-source terms live next to the data they govern — in the builder that
produced the file and on that instance's `sources.html`. What is **not**
recorded anywhere in this repository, and is therefore a gap in this
inventory rather than a fact it can assert:

- **Leaflet and MapLibre GL licence terms.** Both are permissive open-source projects and neither licence is stated anywhere in this repository. Not asserted here from memory.
- **Photon / Komoot service terms.** Only a privacy-policy link is on file. Photon's rate and attribution terms are not recorded.
- **NYC GeoSearch service terms.** Only a privacy-policy link is on file.
- **Nominatim Usage Policy.** Not cited, though the Illinois POI geocoder's worksheet posture (a serial queue at one second or more) is consistent with it.

Each of those is re-audited on every run: if the repository starts
recording one, this build **fails** rather than going on calling it absent.
Most of the government feature services above carry no recorded licence
either. What *is* recorded per host is the **access posture** — the
robots.txt reading, the client measurements, the `blocked` flags — which is
a different question from a licence grant.
